thread:
anya: FYI support ticket from GreenLeaf — they need lower-latency partial responses for chat with tool calls and structured outputs. says current UX stalls while the model finishes the full tool payload. requesting a short-term workaround + product path to support streaming function/tool results as structured chunks. ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/GL-12345 :link:

support-bot: New ticket GL-12345 created by @anya. Priority: P2. SLA: enterprise. Attachments: transcript, repro script.

matt_p: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro of what they get today and what they want? Also any signal on whether they'd accept a documented workaround vs needing a platform change? :thinking:

anya: repro snippet from their integration logs:
```
REQUEST: chat.complete({model: "rwd-small", prompt: "Find last order", tools: [search]})
RESPONSE: stream complete arrives only after search result assembled -> UI waits 3s+
EXPECTED: incremental tool result chunks streamed early -> tokens appear as they come
```
They said they'd tolerate a config flag if it was gated & labeled experimental. They also said they'd pay for an SLA if we ship fully.

kim_e: quick notes from runtime side: we already support incremental token streaming for text. The gap is that our tool-call serialization waits for the entire tool payload (structured JSON) before flushing. Two approaches:
1) Short-term: emit partial tool payloads as escaped text chunks (no structured events) so UI can render earlier. Low infra changes.
2) Long-term: extend the streaming contract to support typed partial events (i.e. event: tool_chunk, meta: {tool, seq}). Requires API contract change + console/docs + SDK updates.
Which does product prefer for backlog?

matt_p: Good summary. For prioritization we need clear acceptance criteria and launch buckets. My initial thought:
- Quick patch (A): experimental opt-in flag `stream_partial_tool_payload` that streams raw chunks as text. Acceptance: reproduce GL-12345 perf improvement in staging + doc + SDK example. Timebox 2w.
- Feature (B): official structured streaming for tool calls (v1). Acceptance: stable SDKs for node/python, console tracing of partial events, backwards compatibility, rollout plan. Target: Q3 milestone.

felix_sales: GL is willing to sign a short-term paid pilot if we can promise <500ms first-byte for tool responses in their main flow. They need it in 6 weeks. If quick patch achieves it, they'll take it.

kim_e: implementation notes for patch A: add runtime switch to bypass waiting for JSON end; stream chunks as:
```
--rwd-stream--
{"__partial_tool":true,"tool":"search","chunk_seq":1,"text":"..."}
--rwd-stream--
```
This keeps a delimited format so SDK can parse without a protocol overhaul. SDKs would need a fast-mode parser.

matt_p: Ok. Risks? backwards compatibility? metrics?

kim_e: risk of clients mis-parsing -> wrap behind opt-in flag, default off. Metrics: new metric `tool.partial_stream_ratio` and `tool.first_byte_latency`. Add logging for malformed frames.

anya: support asks: can we have a short FAQ + sample Node snippet so they can try the opt-in in staging this week? Also need an internal triage note so support knows when to escalate.

matt_p: Action items:
- kim_e: POC for opt-in patch + perf test (due in 7 days)
- anya: sample Node + support FAQ draft (3 days)
- felix_sales: confirm GL pilot contract terms and timeline (5 days)
I'll slot this as "candidate" in the API backlog with tag: customer-critical and note the pilot. If POC looks good we move to near-term ship (A). :rocket:

felix_sales: noted. I'll push for pilot approval and share customer acceptance criteria back here. :+1:

anya: adding short triage note to GL ticket and flagging support docs. Thanks all.

matt_p: leaving this thread with owners. Reopen here with test results or if engineering hits blockers.
